task_title: Tier-1 secrets fails on gitignored bytecode
task_criteria: Fix the tier-1 secrets false positive without blunting the scanner. Four facts must hold: (1) gitleaks detect --no-git run from /home/kara/code-factory reports no leaks with generated __pycache__ bytecode present, and the .gitleaks.toml allowlist entry for bytecode is the reason; (2) a control arm proves the same config still reports a synthetic PEM placed OUTSIDE __pycache__ (e.g. a .py file), so the allowlist is scoped, not a mute; (3) tests/selftest.sh owns the property with an arm that generates a .pyc carrying a PEM marker and requires a clean gitleaks run, prints a named SKIP when the gitleaks binary is absent, and FAILs if the allowlist entry is removed; (4) docs/handbook/chapters/M3-repository.md section 3 submodule S3, the gitleaks rules row in section 5, and the section 7 verification table name the exclusion and why tier-1 scans the working tree. Verify by running the commands and quoting their output. Do not run the full tests/selftest.sh suite as the criterion; grade the four facts from the files and targeted commands.

tier2.summary:
COMPLETE
  ✓ Fix the tier-1 secrets false positive without blunting the scanner. Four facts must hold: (1) gitleaks detect --no-git run from /home/kara/code-factory reports no leaks with generated __pycache__ bytecode present, and the .gitleaks.toml allowlist entry for bytecode is the reason; (2) a control arm proves the same config still reports a synthetic PEM placed OUTSIDE __pycache__ (e.g. a .py file), so the allowlist is scoped, not a mute; (3) tests/selftest.sh owns the property with an arm that generates a .pyc carrying a PEM marker and requires a clean gitleaks run, prints a named SKIP when the gitleaks binary is absent, and FAILs if the allowlist entry is removed; (4) docs/handbook/chapters/M3-repository.md section 3 submodule S3, the gitleaks rules row in section 5, and the section 7 verification table name the exclusion and why tier-1 scans the working tree. Verify by running the commands and quoting their output. Do not run the full tests/selftest.sh suite as the criterion; grade the four facts from the files and targeted commands.: All four facts verified with live output. FACT 1: `cd /home/kara/code-factory && gitleaks detect --no-git --no-banner --redact` -> EXIT=0, 'INF scanned ~2968297 bytes (2.97 MB)', 'INF no leaks found', with 6 .pyc files present in tests/__pycache__ (incl. test_node_provisioning.cpython-314.pyc). Causation proven: copied .gitleaks.toml+tests to /tmp/cf383a, stripped the two entries via grep -vxF, re-ran -> EXIT=1, 'WRN leaks found: 1', JSON report `private-key tests/__pycache__/test_node_provisioning.cpython-314.pyc 35` — the exact original finding, so the allowlist entry is the reason. .gitleaks.toml:57-58 holds `'''__pycache__/'''` and `'''\.pyc$'''` with a CF-383 comment naming the reason; all pre-existing entries retained. FACT 2: /tmp/cf383b with PEM in tests/__pycache__/fixture.cpython-314.pyc + anchor.py -> EXIT=0, 'scanned ~18 bytes', report `[]`; same PEM written to tests/plain.py -> EXIT=1, 'WRN leaks found: 1', report `private-key tests/plain.py 1` — scoped, not a mute. FACT 3: tests/selftest.sh:1954-2041 section 34; ran the arm in isolation (extracted lines 1954-2041, NOT the full suite) -> 'PASS bytecode-allowlist — a PEM in tests/__pycache__/*.pyc yields no finding (18 bytes graded)', 'PASS bytecode-allowlist-control', 'PASS bytecode-allowlist-loadbearing', FAILS=0. SKIP path: ran with PATH=/tmp/nogitleaks (no gitleaks) -> 'SKIP bytecode-allowlist — gitleaks absent from PATH, tier-1 secrets not measurable here' (named SKIP, not a silent pass). FAIL-on-removal: temporarily stripped the two entries from the real .gitleaks.toml and re-ran -> 'FAIL bytecode-allowlist — a PEM in tests/__pycache__/*.pyc was graded as a secret (exit 1, 131 bytes graded)', FAILS=1; config restored, `git status --porcelain` empty. Anti-vacuity guard requires graded bytes > 0 (18 bytes graded). FACT 4: docs/handbook/chapters/M3-repository.md:40 (§3 submodule S3 row) names the bytecode exclusion (`'''__pycache__/'''`, `'''\.pyc$'''`, `:57-58`) and states 'tier-1 grades the working tree (gitleaks detect --no-git) while the commit guard grades staged files only'; :83 (§5 settings register, `.gitleaks.toml` `[allowlist].paths` row) names the exclusion, the reason, and that deleting the entries reds `bytecode-allowlist-loadbearing`; :114-115 (§7 verification table) carry the 'tier-1 secrets scope' row ('no leaks found', exit 0, working tree vs staged files) and the 'bytecode allowlist arm (shipped)' row naming all three arms.
